newsitem.title: PANAMA: US officer in Panama charged in death of soldier.
newsitem.headline: US officer in Panama charged in death of soldier.

text.p: A U.S. Army officer has been charged with involuntary manslaughter following the death of a soldier who collapsed during a routine training exercise in Panama last month, the Army said on Tuesday.

Chief Warrant Officer Kyle Grogan, 31, was charged on Monday with involuntary manslaughter, negligent homicide, maltreatment of a subordinate and dereliction of duty because of the March 4 death of Sgt. Edward Palacio, 27, Army South spokesman Maj. Joe Curtain said. Army South is a component of the U.S. Southern Command forces based in Panama.

An investigation has been ordered and could take up to three weeks to decide whether Grogan, who was suspended from his duties, will face a court-martial, Curtain said. He said Palacio died at a hospital in San Antonio, Texas, apparently from complications from heat stroke during a routine physical training exercise on March 1 in which Grogan took part.
Curtain said Palacio was taken to Wilford Hall Medical Centre after collapsing during the exercise on the running trails at Howard Air Force Base, near the Pacific Ocean entrance of the Panama Canal.
"He was rushed to the hospital for heat problems, basically heat stroke. When his condition worsened we medically evacuated him to Texas within 48 hours. On March 4 the soldier died," he said.
Grogan, who was assigned to a special operations aviation regiment at Fort Kobbe in Panama, is a 13-year veteran from Kermit, Texas.
